beats.text: There is no evidence Marie Antoinette ever said let them eat cake.
beats.note: Historians treat the line as a cliché that was attached to her later.

beats.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
beats.role: Wrote the line in his Confessions about an unnamed great princess, and may have invented the anecdote. It was published in 1782.

beats.text: When Rousseau wrote it, Marie Antoinette was nine years old.
beats.note: She had not yet left Austria. She did not arrive in France until 1770.

beats.text: The French word is brioche, a luxury bread enriched with butter and eggs.
beats.note: Cake is the traditional English translation.

beats.name: Alphonse Karr
beats.role: A French writer who attributed the line to Marie Antoinette in print, about fifty years after her death.

beats.line: The quote is older than the queen.
